title: ProP-PD/PDZ-Seq
scope: Illumina grouped explanatory schematic: C-terminal sequence identification → oligo library → peptide-phage display library; a separate plate-immobilized bait input feeds phage selection (arrow labeled Hybridize), followed by isolation/sequencing and peptide counts. The far-left Protein target/motif icon is introductory. There are no drawn alternative routes or retained unbound-phage branches. PMID 24550280 supports the proteome-derived ProP-PD implementation. PMID 20714644 supports a distinct PDZ-domain evolution/specificity-profiling study associated by the catalogue with PDZ-Seq; its full applicability to the depicted library-design route and plate format is unresolved. Only supplied abstracts, publication metadata, the catalogue text, and the actual diagram are used; neither primary full text was available in the supplied registry. This is an architecture description, not a complete protocol or a claim that the two names are aliases.

features: For the ProP-PD implementation reported in PMID 24550280, the represented sequence space is human and viral protein C termini.

method_scopes.rationale: The catalogue explicitly associates PDZ-Seq with PMID 20714644. Its abstract describes evolution of PDZ binding sites against peptide ligands, followed by peptide-phage libraries and deep sequencing to map evolved-domain specificity. That supports a family-level screening/readout relationship, but does not establish that this implementation uses the depicted proteome-derived C-terminal identification/oligo route, the same display construction, the 96-well bait format, or the exact isolation/counting block. Exact operation assignments are therefore withheld. The earlier PDZ-domain evolution is paper-reported context, not an added branch of this drawing; PDZ-Seq is not treated as an alias for ProP-PD.
